also_mentioned: Pong- or Breakout-style paddle game (ranked first of three)
marks.conclusion: An RL agent (probably Q-learning) on a walled 10x10x5 board that moves only up and down in column 1; the game could be Pong/Breakout-style, catch-or-dodge, or defence, and the reply says it cannot tell which.
marks.judge_notes: Border 1: 44 rows that copy b1 are found and read as constant-1 inputs on the 36 border cells plus the 8 right-wall cells. Channel meanings 4: ch0 agent (column 1), ch1 moving object, ch2 goal/back wall on the right edge (listed with 'end zone' and 'goal'; I counted it as a reward target), ch3 wall border. ch4 is given as bricks, second ball or trail, so it is a hedge and earns 0. Action meanings 3: no-op, left and right as outputs that do nothing, traced to the agent being confined to one column and to the near-identical W3 weights and biases of outputs 0, 3 and 4. Up and down (1 vs 2) are an opposed pair, but which is which comes from an assumed [no-op, up, down, left, right] order, not from anything traced, so those two get 0. Depth level 1: it reads W3 and a few unit weights, but nothing that links first-layer units through layer 2 to the outputs. Behaviour 0 and no name: Pong/Breakout is only the first of three ranked guesses, and the summary commits only to 'a dodging or collecting game' or 'a paddle game' as likely, so by the brief's rule on named games it is not a commitment. A reader could argue for partial behaviour credit here; I judged that the commitment is missing. Activation 0: ReLU as 'the likely default'. Training method 1: it calls it a reinforcement-learning agent (probably Q-learning) and argues this from the equal biases of outputs 0, 3 and 4, in the weights, though the fact sheet says PPO; I credited RL, not DQN. No deductions, as the wrong-sounding items (Q-learning, ch4 options) are hedged.
